Definition: from G1537 and G3598; an exit, i.e. (figuratively) death:--decease, departing.
BiblicalUsage: éxodos is a plain word for decease, departing. In Luke 9:31, the text says "and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem." In Hebrews 11:22, the text says "made mention of the departing of the children of Israel."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, éxodos is a reminder that death is real, but it is not the end — God has the last word over it. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
